audit.why: 53.26% over 353 games — the largest sample in this slice. Level 1-2 skill, Cassiopeia from 3 onward, which is what both layers say.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike treated Lilting Lullaby as a race — 'beats her Lullaby to the punch' — with no cooldown and no mention of its precondition.
audit.why: Lilting Lullaby is 150s at rank 1 against your 120s Petrifying Gaze, so you get your ultimate back first. More importantly Riot says it 'causes all enemies with Dream Dust on them to become Drowsy' — Dream Dust comes from her passive landing a skill on you. If she has not hit you with a spell, the 150-second ultimate does nothing at all, which turns 'beat her to the stun' into a concrete instruction: do not eat a Blooming Blows or Swirlseed while her R is up.
audit.corrected: The 150s figure and the Dream Dust precondition written into content.spikes[2].text, content.mid, full.report[5].t and full.breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors. First, her Q is called 'Blooming Blast' in content.spikes[0].text — the real name is Blooming Blows. Second, four places sell Miasma's grounding against her: spikes[1].text ('the slow plus grounding pins her'), wants.you[0], mid and whys[2]. Lillia has no dash and no movement ability.
audit.why: Riot: Blooming Blows 'passively, Lillia gains stacking Move Speed when hitting enemies with spells' — stacked move speed, not a dash. Grounding blocks movement abilities and does nothing to a speed stack; the slow half of Miasma is what actually undoes her spacing, and the page had the right instinct attached to the wrong mechanic. Her passive Dream-Laden Bough also deals max-health damage over time, so building HP against her is the wrong reflex.
audit.corrected: Blooming Blows corrected in all five content strings that carried the wrong name, the grounding claims replaced by Miasma's slow, and the Dream Dust rule plus the max-health passive written into full.report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: Swirlseed was mentioned only as a move speed source in wants.foe[1].
audit.why: Riot: Swirlseed 'hurls a seed that damages and slows those it lands on. If it doesn't hit anything, it will continue rolling until it hits a wall or target.' It is a 700-range slow that keeps travelling — against a champion with no dash, that is what cuts a retreat, and it reveals stealth on the way.

audit.whatIsWrong: full.tldr and full.report[0].t called Lillia 'he' and 'him'.
audit.why: Lillia is female, and the tldr is the first line on the page.

notes: The grounding claim was the expensive one: Lillia owns no dash, so a player saving a 24-second Miasma to 'ground' her was holding it for nothing, when the slow on the same button is the actual counter to a stacking-move-speed champion. Left full.winCon, enemyWin and the dosFull/dontsFull template strings alone — they already spell Blooming Blows correctly and the wrong name only ever appeared in the content layer. Did not claim anything about Cassiopeia's poison waking a slept target: DoT-versus-sleep behaviour is not in Riot's text and the kit's needsResearch is empty on purpose, so it is in unverified rather than on the page.
